subject: Temporary Cross-Region Authorization & Subprocessor Escrow Plan
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@cloudmed.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cloudmed.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary cross-region processing window & subprocessors

Hi Ben,

Quick context: CloudMed is onboarding Redwood for clinical note embeddings. Our legal and security teams ran the DPA and asked for a narrow temporary cross-region processing allowance for a short disaster-recovery window during the EU cutover (anticipated for next month). Specifically:

- We need a documented process that allows up to 72 hours of transient processing in the US for a small subset of tenant traffic if EU capacity is degraded.
- An explicit list of subprocessors that may be involved during that window (or a binding escrow mechanism if you rotate subprocessors).
- Confirmation of KMS handling for any keys used during the window (we prefer no key material export outside EU).

Can you share a draft DPA addendum and an operational checklist (who to notify, rollback, timelines) we can review with our SOC and procurement teams? Procurement also asked for a doc they can attach to the purchase order.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Information Security, CloudMed Systems
attachments: none

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice@cloudmed.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary cross-region processing window & subprocessors

Alice — thanks for the clear ask and context. High level: we can support a 72-hour transient processing window under a DPA addendum and an operational escrow for subprocessors, with these guardrails:

- Scope: applies only to production inference traffic for the specified CloudMed tenant ID; telemetry/analytics remain EU-only unless specifically consented.
- Duration: max 72 continuous hours per incident; auto-rollback to EU when capacity recovers.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a signed escrow roster of subprocessors that might be used during failover. Any unlisted subprocessor requires a 7-day notice and customer approval for this customer.
- KMS: we do not export customer key material out of the EU. For temporary routing we support a dual-key approach: customer-managed KMS with a transient key policy or Redwood-managed per-tenant key stored in an EU-only key ring; in either case, we can provide key-thumbprint verification and audit logs.

I've attached a draft DPA addendum (DPA_addendum_v2.pdf) and an escrow roster CSV with the current subprocessors that would be eligible. Kimberly, can you confirm the KMS wording and provide the operations checklist for notification and rollback? Lauren, can you flag any procurement language we should include for PO attachment?

Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: DPA_addendum_v2.pdf (pdf), escrow-subprocessor-roster.csv (csv)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alice Zhang <alice@cloudmed.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 14:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary cross-region processing window & subprocessors

Alice, Ben — adding the ops + KMS details below. I pulled in input from Infra and Security.

Operational checklist (short form):
- Trigger: EU region health below 60% for >10 minutes OR SEV incident declared by Redwood ops.
- Authorization: Customer security contact (Alice or designated DPO) must acknowledge within 30 minutes. If no ack, auto-escalate to Redwood on-call and apply the pre-authorized transient window (per addendum).
- Notification cadence: initial notification (email + PagerDuty) -> hourly status updates -> incident close summary within 24 hours of rollback.
- Rollback: automatic routing back to EU when healthy capacity >=80% sustained for 15 minutes; ops will run cache invalidation and a short KV resync (typically <10 minutes).
- Audit evidence: we will provide a post-incident bundle: timeline, routing logs, token-level latency/cost summary, and KMS audit events.

KMS specifics:
- No customer key material leaves the EU. For CloudMed we recommend customer-managed keys in an EU KMS tenant. Redwood can perform envelope encryption in EU and only store transient session keys in memory in the US during the 72h window; those session keys are ephemeral and irrecoverable once the session terminates.
- If you prefer Redwood-managed keys, we will generate per-tenant keys in EU-only HSMs and rotate on incident closure.

Procurement language suggestion (short):
"Redwood may temporarily route inference requests to alternate regions for up to 72 hours to preserve service availability; such routing will be narrowly scoped to the Customer's tenant, use EU-resident key material only, and be governed by the DPA addendum attached."

I'll attach the operations checklist and the KMS wording as a small addendum. Ben/Lauren: I'll drop the DocuSign link once legal confirms the final redlines.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
attachments: ops-checklist.txt (text)

Ben / Kimberly — this looks good and addresses most of our asks. A couple of small follow-ups before procurement will sign:

1) Subprocessor escrow: please confirm the CSV includes the operational contact and SOC attestation snapshot for each subprocessor (we need a per-entry "SOC 2 type II / date" column).
2) DocuSign: procurement requested a single DocuSign package that includes the DPA addendum and the procurement clause as one attachment. Can you send that link?
3) KMS: CloudMed will keep customer-managed KMS in the EU. We need the exact audit event keys Redwood will provide post-incident (e.g., key create, key use, key destroy, wrapped-key-thumbprint).

If those are included, we expect to sign within 48 hours. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

—Alice
Alice Zhang
Head of Information Security, CloudMed Systems
